content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge compares the challenger's and defender's chains by footing in a D6-versus-C1 collision, so K-C governs the way the collision must be weighed.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse — whether it bars any explicit-naming test at the chain level, or only bars resolving the collision by one verse's contrary wording.","why":"The judge treats the challenger chain's failure to name Joseph as a reason for underdetermination even though the chain is footed, which is the explicit-statement test K-C forbids in a chain-against-chain collision."}
